title: The Burning Ember
premise: Oscar Dravenmoor has spent a decade mapping the Thornfell mountains and keeping her true identity—the last heir of the Ember Covenant—buried beneath ink and anonymity. When the old gods stir and answer prayers for the first time in three centuries, the fragile seal between the mortal realm and the god-realm of Vaelith begins to crack, unleashing hungry remnants of forgotten divinity. Hunted by the Crown's Inquisitors who want the covenant destroyed forever, and guided by a found family of smugglers, exiles, and one very inconvenient fallen priest named Cassian Vale, Oscar must reforge the broken covenant at the Ember Altar before the solstice. She succeeds only by sacrificing her own godhood-inheritance, choosing mortal love and chosen family over absolute power—and discovering that a covenant reforged by choice, not blood, holds stronger than the old one ever did.
about_author: Mara Fairweather is the pen name of a former trail guide turned novelist who once spent a winter mapping cave systems in the Carpathians. She writes fantasy about people who would rather stay lost than be found.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Rule
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Establishes her meticulous double life: by day she sells maps to merchants, by night she memorizes smuggler routes no map should hold. A tremor shakes Thornfell's peaks—an earthquake, she assumes. Emotional beat: comfortable isolation beginning to feel like a cage.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Village girl Wren's POV. Wren prays to a dead god for rain and it rains—black rain that whispers names. The village turns on her as a witch. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear; introduces the supernatural stakes through innocent eyes.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Salt Road
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She finds Wren half-dead on the mountain pass and, against every rule of invisibility, saves her. Wren carries a brand shaped like an ember that won't heal. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Gilded Inquisitor
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Seraphine Locke's POV. Locke arrives in the border town hunting 'god-touched' heretics, burning a shrine as a warning. She possesses a fragment of the old covenant seal. Emotional beat: chilling conviction—we meet a villain who believes she's saving the world.

chapters.title: Smoke Over Thornfell
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Soldiers raze the waystation where Oscar keeps her secret archive of pre-Covenant maps. She escapes with only her father's journal, which hints at the Ember Covenant and her bloodline. Emotional beat: grief and the death of her hidden life.

chapters.title: The Hollow Lantern
chapters.summary: Cassian Vale's POV. Introduces the disgraced priest drinking in a smugglers' den, haunted by the night his prayers were answered with silence. He recognizes the ember-brand when he sees Oscar's map-work. Emotional beat: shame seeking redemption.

chapters.title: What the Journal Buried
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Deciphering her father's journal, she learns the Dravenmoors were covenant-keepers who bound the gods after the Sundering—and that the binding is failing because the bloodline thinned. Emotional beat: fury at generations of lies.

chapters.title: Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the smuggler haven of Duskhollow, Wren bonds with the crew: one-eyed pilot Brannoc, twin forgers Ilsa and Petra, and gruff matriarch Mother Quill. Emotional beat: warmth—found family assembling around a frightened child.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. To reach the first altar site, she must bargain with the Ferryman of the Greywater, who demands a memory as toll. She pays with her mother's face. Emotional beat: sacrifice establishing what the quest will cost.

chapters.title: Gods in the Gutters
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. A minor god—a beggar-king of lost coins—manifests in Duskhollow, drawn to Wren's brand. It speaks Oscar's name before dissolving. Emotional beat: dread; the gods know who she is.

chapters.title: Locke's Ledger
chapters.summary: Seraphine's POV. Interrogating a captured smuggler, Locke learns of a 'map-witch' in Thornfell and connects her to the extinct Dravenmoor line. Her superiors order the bloodline erased. Emotional beat: hunter closing in.

chapters.title: The First Altar
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the drowned shrine of Vess, Oscar performs the first rite of renewal using her blood. It works—but something on the other side notices her. Emotional beat: awe and terror entwined.

chapters.title: Ash and Argument
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Cassian confronts Oscar about hiding her identity from the crew; their fight sparks into reluctant intimacy. He confesses his failed prayers. Emotional beat: walls cracking between two guarded people.

chapters.title: The God That Hungers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A remnant god called the Maw devours a mining town, wearing the faces of the eaten. Wren's brand burns, pulling the Maw toward her. Emotional beat: horror; the stakes are now flesh and bone.

chapters.title: Running the Teeth
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A desperate chase through the smuggler roads Oscar knows best, using unmapped ways to outrun the Maw. Brannoc loses his ship saving them. Emotional beat: the cost of loyalty; the crew becomes family in earnest.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Seraphine's POV. Locke captures Mother Quill and offers her mercy for information. Quill gives nothing but contempt and dies unbroken. Emotional beat: rage and resolve; the enemy shows her cruelty.

chapters.title: The Second Altar
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the cliffside shrine of Aurel, the rite demands a truth spoken aloud. Oscar admits she wants the power, not just the duty. The seal strengthens anyway. Emotional beat: honesty as strength.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Cassian reads his old seminary letters and realizes the Church knew the covenant was failing for decades and chose silence. Emotional beat: disillusionment deepening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Court of Cinders
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Pulled through the thinning veil, Oscar stands briefly in Vaelith among the diminished gods, who offer her full inheritance of power if she abandons the slow, mortal path. Emotional beat: temptation made gorgeous.

chapters.title: Refusal and Ruin
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren witnesses Oscar refuse the gods—and the Maw uses her moment of vulnerability to mark Wren fully. The crew realizes the child is bait. Emotional beat: protective love hardening into strategy.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Map That Maps Itself
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Her father's final page reveals a living map that redraws itself toward the Ember Altar—but only for a willing heir. It also reveals a third party seeks the altar: the Church itself means to kill the covenant permanently. Emotional beat: the race reframed—two enemies, one road.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Weeping Stair
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Locke's Inquisitors ambush the party on the mountain stair. Cassian takes a blade meant for Oscar; Ilsa dies holding the pass. Emotional beat: devastating loss; love confessed in blood.

chapters.title: Triage and Truth
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Tending Cassian's wound, Oscar tells him everything—her name, her blood, her fear. He chooses to stay. Emotional beat: vulnerability rewarded; the romance solidifies into partnership.

chapters.title: Locke's Doubt
chapters.summary: Seraphine's POV. Examining Ilsa's body, Locke finds proof the Church's own rites caused the Sundering. Her certainty fractures. Emotional beat: the antagonist's crisis of faith begins.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Toll
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. One of the Duskhollow crew, bought by the Church, sabotages their supplies. Petra catches him; the family must decide his fate. They exile him rather than kill him. Emotional beat: mercy as a deliberate, costly choice.

chapters.title: Winterhold's Bargain
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Seeking allies, Oscar petitions the mountain clans, who demand she prove her blood by surviving the Trial of Embers—a walk through living flame. Emotional beat: courage tested publicly; she emerges marked but accepted.

chapters.title: The Clanmother's Secret
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The clanmother reveals the Dravenmoors didn't bind the gods to save the world—they bound them to seize their power. Oscar's inheritance is stolen goods. Emotional beat: the hero's legacy poisoned; identity shaken.

chapters.title: What Power Wants
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Alone, Oscar feels the inherited power whispering its appetites. She nearly uses it to erase her doubts—and stops herself by gripping Cassian's hand. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; corruption resisted by connection.

chapters.title: The Third Altar Falls
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. They arrive at the third shrine to find it annihilated—by Church fire, not god-hunger. Without all three altars, the covenant cannot be renewed the traditional way. Emotional beat: despair; the plan collapses.

chapters.title: Locke Defects
chapters.summary: Seraphine's POV. Locke refuses an order to burn a village of god-touched children and is branded a heretic herself. She flees toward the mountains, carrying the stolen seal-fragment. Emotional beat: antagonist becoming unlikely ally.

chapters.title: Uneasy Hands
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Locke reaches the camp; knives come out. Oscar accepts her help because the fragment is essential, but trust is rationed drop by drop. Emotional beat: tension of alliance without forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Maw Ascendant
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Maw consumes the Greywater Ferryman and grows vast enough to tear the veil wide. Wren understands the brand isn't a curse—it's a key. Emotional beat: the hunted child realizing she is the answer.

chapters.title: The Living Map
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The self-drawing map completes itself: the true Ember Altar was never in a shrine—it's beneath Thornfell itself, in the mountain's heart, reachable only by the smuggler roads only Oscar knows. Emotional beat: her invisible life revealed as preparation all along.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. The company descends through the mountain's roots while the Maw hunts them through the dark. Brannoc stays behind to collapse a tunnel on it, buying hours. Emotional beat: sacrifice stacking; dread thickening.

chapters.title: The Ember Altar
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the heart-mountain altar, the rite demands what the old Dravenmoors never paid: the heir must give up the power itself, renouncing godhood forever. The Maw breaches the chamber. Emotional beat: the choice distilled—power or people.

chapters.title: Climax: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV (with intercut POVs). Oscar pours her inheritance into the altar, unbinding the stolen power and returning it to the gods freely. The Maw, offered its own name back instead of hunger, dissolves into rain. Wren's brand fades. Emotional beat: transcendence through surrender; the covenant remade on consent.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Ash
chapters.summary: Seraphine's POV. Locke returns to the Church to testify against her superiors, knowing it will likely destroy her. She and Oscar part as something like equals. Emotional beat: justice begun, redemption unfinished.

chapters.title: Maps Worth Drawing
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Spring comes. Cassian and Oscar rebuild Duskhollow, and he asks her—not to stop mapping, but to map with him. Emotional beat: quiet joy; love chosen without duty's shadow.

chapters.title: Wren's First Prayer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren prays again—this time simply thanks—and the sky answers with ordinary sunlight. She begins training as the new covenant's first witness. Emotional beat: healing; the next generation entrusted.

chapters.title: The Unmapped Country
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Epilogue. Oscar draws a new map of Thornfell and leaves one region deliberately blank, labeled 'for whatever comes next.' The ember on the horizon glows steady, not hungry. Emotional beat: peace earned, mystery preserved, story closed.
